newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ENERGY AFRICA TO DOUBLE OUTPUT IN TWO YRS.
newsitem.headline: ENERGY AFRICA TO DOUBLE OUTPUT IN TWO YRS.

text.p: Specialist oil exploration and production company Energy Africa Ltd said on Thursday it expected to double crude oil production over the next two years.
The former upstream arm of Engen Ltd, with interests in West and Southern Africa, registered a 20 percent increase in output to an average 6,700 barrels per day (bpd) in the year to August 31, 1996.

Since then production has increased further and the company said it recently broke through the 10,000 bpd level, reflecting additional flows from the Alba field in the North Sea and Nkossa offshore Congo, which commenced production in June 1996.

Energy Africa, still 60.5 percent owned by Engen, was floated on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in March 1996 and managing director John Bentley said performance since then had exceeded expectations, helped by high oil prices and a weak rand.
Net cash flow from operations in the year to August 31 surged 92 percent from the 1994/95 level to 115 million rand -- 33 percent up on projections made at the time of the listing.

For the current year, Bentley said he expected strong operational cash flow from a full year's output from the Nkossa field, in which it has a 2.25 percent stake, and increased production from Alba, where it holds eight percent.

In addition, Energy Africa will get the benefit of a slice of production from South Africa's first oil field, Oribi, which is due to start pumping at 20,000 bpd in February. Energy Africa has a 20 percent share in the offshore field.

On the exploration front, Energy Africa drilled ten wells over the year of which five hit potentially commercial hydrocarbon accumulations, three were dry and two were still in progress at the year-end.

"We expect to participate in the drilling of eight to ten exploration and appraisal wells on existing licences during the current financial year. All but one of these are situated in West Africa," said Bentley.
Looking ahead, Bentley said the listing of Energy Africa had raised the group's profile and the company was well-placed for partnerships with majors interested in developing African prospects.
The recent acquisition by Malaysian state oil company Petronas of a 30 percent stake in parent Engen also offered the prospect of co-operation in new ventures.
"I think the association will allow us to do joint ventures with them, particularly in North Africa where they have extremely good relationships with governments," Bentley said.
